scope: Oral rentosertib and proteomic biological-age markers in IPF. Not general human rejuvenation or longevity.
limits: The proteomic clocks cannot separate aging biology from improvement in IPF.
Biomarker changes do not establish longer life or reversed aging.
The single retained registry trial measures safety and lung function; its secondary proteomic analysis is identified by the primary paper.

retained_trials.reason: The primary aging-clock paper explicitly identifies this trial; its complete proteomic subset has 42 participants out of 71 enrolled.

excluded_trials.reason: Phase 3 IPF trial includes general serum proteomics, but its record does not specify biological-age clocks. Insufficient evidence for this narrower claim; exclusion is not proof the study could never support it.
Separate US Phase 2a IPF trial. The 2025 abstract mentions future antifibrotic biomarker validation, but no verified aging-clock analysis links this trial to the narrow claim.

paper_exclusion_reason: Inhaled formulation studies, not the oral proteomic-ageing report. First three were tentative; last was rule approved. All excluded through normal assistant review.
